lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 4: Adversarial Robustness and Generative Models

unit.name: Why diffusion and how forward noising works
unit.description: Motivates diffusion as a non-adversarial alternative to GANs and defines the forward diffusion process that progressively adds Gaussian noise to data.
unit.summary: Diffusion is motivated by two GAN limitations: mode collapse, where G covers only a narrow subset of outputs, and instability from training two coupled models simultaneously [ts=4597s]. The instructor uses diffusion-versus-GAN examples to argue that diffusion can produce more variety and better coverage of a real distribution, such as single and grouped flamingos or more varied burgers [ts=4650s]. A diffusion model avoids the minimax game by training one model on a denoising task designed to model the entire data distribution with more stable gradients [ts=4714s]. The forward diffusion process starts from a clean image x0 and progressively adds Gaussian noise until the picture is no longer recognizable [ts=4880s]. In the simplified recurrence, x_{t+1} is x_t plus Gaussian noise, and x_t can be viewed as x0 plus cumulative noise that must later be predicted [ts=4932s].

key_points.text: Diffusion is introduced to avoid GAN mode collapse and adversarial training instability.
Diffusion examples show greater variety than GAN examples, suggesting broader coverage of the data distribution.
Diffusion models progressively add noise to data and learn to reverse the process.
The forward process takes x0 through noisy states up to xT by adding more noise at each time step.
In the simplified formula, x_{t+1} = x_t + epsilon_t with epsilon_t drawn from Gaussian noise.

kp_catalog.name: GAN instability diagnostics
kp_catalog.description: GAN value and loss curves are not reliable progress indicators because the game is non-stationary and jointly adversarial.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Important because gAN instability diagnostics clarifies gAN value and loss curves are not reliable progress indicators because the game is non-stationary and jointly adversarial, sharpening later modeling, analysis, or evaluation choices.

kp_catalog.name: Forward diffusion process
kp_catalog.description: A noising process that transforms clean data into increasingly noisy states by adding Gaussian noise over time, creating the supervised signal for denoising.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Forward diffusion is foundational within diffusion models, but should support the broader diffusion-denoising gateway.
